name: temporary-http-share-v1
description: Temporary HTTP shares: a revocable, expiring grant for one protected HTTP route, reached under /http-share/{shareId}/ with an HttpOnly cookie that holds the share token. Covers creation, the fragment-to-cookie exchange, the decision for every request under the share path, revocation, the lifecycle events that end shares, the expiry sweep, audit entries, header rewriting and rate limits. See protocol/spec/temporary-http-share.md.
notes: now 未给出时为 2026-10-06T08:00:00Z；所有时刻精确到秒，expiresAt 严格：now >= expiresAt 即已过期。
共享的初始世界见 world：租户 t1 有管理员 admin 与 carol、普通用户 alice 与 bob；alice 拥有客户端 7（路由 42 名为 api 且受保护、43 公开、44 停用），bob 拥有客户端 8（路由 50 受保护）；租户 t2 有管理员 eve。input.worldChanges 是用例在此基础上的改动（deleted 表示该行被删除）。
input.shares 是存储中的分享行；tokenSha256 是完整 token 字符串 UTF-8 的 SHA-256 小写十六进制，明文 token 不入库。
create 用例中新分享的 shareId 与 token 由测试注入的随机源决定，取 newShare 中的固定值；实现应注入同样的字节。

access 用例的 expect.httpStatus 为 forwarded 时表示请求按 route 语义转发给设备，forward 给出 NAT OPEN 中的 route（route 当前的名字）、method、relativePath、rawQuery 与转发的 Cookie 头（null 表示不带 Cookie 头）。其余请求头按 http-route.md 处理，Authorization 原样转发。
headers.response 是分享响应在 route 自身响应规则之后追加的改写：relayed 为发给访客的头，顺序有意义；Cache-Control 追加在末尾。
expect.revoke 表示该请求把分享就地撤销（revokedBy 为 null）并写入 expect.audit；之后同一分享的任何请求都是 410。
expect.setCookie 为结构化 cookie：属性顺序不限，不得带 Domain；maxAge 为 0 表示清除。
lifecycle 用例按顺序重放 events；expect.audit 逐条比较 action、at、actor、routeId、shareId 与 detail；auditId 由实现分配，不在向量里。
rate 的每个事件是同一时刻、同一键上连续的 requests 个请求；admitted 是其中放行的个数，retryAfterSeconds 是第一个被拒请求的 Retry-After。被拒请求不消耗额度。

create.name: owner-creates-read-share
create.note: Defaults: read-only, the whole route, no label.

create.name: admin-creates-full-share-with-prefix
create.note: A tenant admin may share any route of the tenant. The prefix gets its trailing slash; the label is trimmed of spaces.

create.name: expiry-above-maximum
create.note: There is no unbounded share: a long-lived grant is what a protected route with its own password is for.

create.name: expiry-missing
create.note: The expiry is mandatory; there is no default.

create.name: unknown-field
create.note: Unknown fields are rejected, so a client cannot believe a limit is enforced when it is not.

create.name: store-unreadable
create.note: A read failure is not reported as a missing route.

create.name: other-owner
create.note: Not the owner and not an admin: indistinguishable from a route that does not exist.

create.name: route-public
create.note: A public route is reachable by anyone already; a share on it would suggest that revoking the share stops access. Protect the route first.

create.name: ended-shares-do-not-count
create.note: Expired and revoked shares do not count against the limit of active shares per route.

exchange.name: valid
exchange.note: The cookie is scoped to the share path and lives exactly as long as the share; the landing page then replaces itself with location.

exchange.name: last-second
exchange.note: One second before expiry: Max-Age is the one second left.

exchange.name: at-expiry
exchange.note: Expiry is strict: at expiresAt the share has ended.

exchange.name: form-post
exchange.note: Only JSON: another site cannot submit the exchange with a plain form.

exchange.name: malformed-token
exchange.note: Charged to the source address like any attempt, answered like an unknown token.

exchange.name: wrong-secret
exchange.note: Same share id, different secret: indistinguishable from a share that does not exist.

exchange.name: revoked
exchange.note: Only someone holding the token learns that the share ended.

exchange.name: lapsed-route-public
exchange.note: The route was made public by a path that did not revoke its shares; the share is revoked now.

access.name: in-scope-get
access.note: The share cookie is removed from the Cookie header; every other cookie and the raw query go to the device unchanged.

access.name: prefix-itself
access.note: The prefix without its trailing slash is in scope; the target may redirect to the slash form.

access.name: only-share-cookie
access.note: No other cookies: the device receives no Cookie header at all.

access.name: missing-trailing-slash
access.note: Decided before any lookup, the same for every well-formed id.

access.name: no-cookie
access.note: No credential: the same answer as a share that does not exist.

access.name: cookie-of-another-share
access.note: A valid token of share B never opens share A.

access.name: planted-cookie-first
access.note: A same-origin page planted a cookie of the same name with a longer Path, so the browser sends it first. The server tries up to four values that name this share.

access.name: token-in-authorization-header
access.note: The token is accepted only from the cookie; Authorization belongs to the target and is relayed unchanged.

access.name: revoked
access.note: The cookie is cleared so the browser stops presenting it.

access.name: expired-and-lapsed
access.note: An expired share is not revoked afterwards: expiry wins and nothing is written.

access.name: admin-share-survives-owner-disabled
access.note: The share belongs to whoever created it: an admin's share does not depend on the owner's account.

access.name: read-share-refuses-websocket
access.note: A WebSocket is a GET that can carry data to the target: not read-only.

access.name: dot-dot-escape
access.note: Encoded dot segments are dot segments.

access.name: literal-dot-dot
access.note: Browsers remove dot segments before sending; a client that does not is refused.

access.name: semicolon
access.note: Servlet containers strip ;parameters and then normalise: refused under a prefix.

access.name: encoded-unreserved-in-scope
access.note: Escapes of unreserved characters are decoded before matching, as the target will decode them; the raw path is forwarded unchanged.

access.name: whole-route-share-has-no-path-rules
access.note: With the prefix / the share covers exactly what the route covers, so the route's own path rules apply and nothing more.

lifecycle.name: owner-revokes-then-revokes-again
lifecycle.note: Revocation is idempotent: the second call answers 200 and writes nothing. Someone who cannot manage the route gets 404, and a share id under a route it does not belong to is not found.

lifecycle.name: route-disabled-ends-every-active-share
lifecycle.note: Disabling revokes; enabling again does not bring the shares back. The already-expired share is not touched.

lifecycle.name: route-made-public
lifecycle.note: A public route needs no share; keeping one would mislead the owner into thinking revoking it stops access.

lifecycle.name: credentials-changed-keeps-shares
lifecycle.note: Changing the Basic password is audited but does not touch shares: they never used it.

lifecycle.name: client-deleted
lifecycle.note: Deleting a client deletes its routes: each gets a route.deleted entry, then the shares end.

lifecycle.name: creator-disabled
lifecycle.note: Only the disabled user's own shares end; the admin's share of the same route stays.

lifecycle.name: admin-demoted
lifecycle.note: An admin who is demoted and owns neither client loses every share it created.

lifecycle.name: owner-promoted-then-demoted-keeps-own-route
lifecycle.note: Still the owner of the client after the demotion: nothing to end.

lifecycle.name: route-created
lifecycle.note: Creating a route is an exposure change too. Turning on Basic for the first time records both the exposure change and the new credentials.

lifecycle.name: sweep-records-expiry-once
lifecycle.note: Each expiry is written once, stamped with expiresAt rather than the sweep time, in expiry order. A share revoked before it expired gets no expiry entry.

lifecycle.name: missed-hook-undone-before-sweep
lifecycle.note: If a change bypassed the hooks and was undone before any request or sweep saw it, the share survives -- the window is one sweep interval. Here the sweep runs after the undo: nothing to do.

lifecycle.name: sweep-revokes-a-lapsed-share
lifecycle.note: The sweep revokes with no actor; protecting the route again does not revive the share.
